solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Snappy dresser, outstanding one in petroleum processing plant

parts.note: in slang a cat is a man, especially a stylish or fashionable one
a cracker is an excellent or outstanding person or thing

explanation.surface: A smartly turned-out worker stands out among the staff at an oil refinery.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat cracker (short for catalytic cracker) is the unit in a refinery that breaks heavy oil into lighter fuels.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat cracker is a refinery installation that splits heavy hydrocarbons using a catalyst, so it is a processing plant.

clue.text: Friend, muddled chap no good with tip in cafe, producing unacceptable one? (11, two words)

definitions.note: the 'one' is a tip, so the phrase describes a measly sum

parts.note: a chum is a friend

indicators.note: something muddled is jumbled up, so the word it describes has its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

indicators.note: a tip is an end point, here the final letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A confused friend leaves a pitiful tip at a cafe, which the waiter finds insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like money left in the cafe, and that is in fact what the whole answer describes: a tip so small it is an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Chump change is a trivial, contemptible sum of money, so a tip of that size would be unacceptable.

clue.text: Backs possibly injured dropped from later game?

indicators.note: letters dropped from a phrase are taken out of it, leaving the rest in place

parts.note: someone lame has an injured leg, one possible kind of injury
taken as written; the answer is not simply hidden here, since letters of the injured word must first be dropped from around it, which is a coincidence of the deletion

explanation.surface: Damaged backs keep a player out of a game later in the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing L, A, M and E from LATER GAME leaves TERGA; the four letters are scattered through the phrase but in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Terga is the plural of tergum, the plate covering the back of an insect or other arthropod segment.

clue.text: Crop that's cold, damp and chilly

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
raw weather is damp and cold

explanation.surface: A harvest is spoilt by cold, wet, chilly weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' reads as a farmer's harvest, but it is the pouch in a bird's gullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A craw is the crop of a bird or insect, the pouch where food is stored before digestion.

clue.text: Indication of hesitancy with vermin around? We'll supply estimates

definitions.note: a phrase standing for people who estimate

indicators.note: the vermin are placed around the sound of hesitancy, enclosing it

parts.note: rats are classic vermin
er is the sound a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: Pest controllers hesitate to price the job when rats are everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Raters are people who assess value or rate things, so they are the ones who supply estimates.

clue.text: Duenna's responsibility, having tea with person approaching maturity

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
per. is the dictionary abbreviation for person
on can mean approaching, as in 'getting on for'
to come of age is to reach maturity

explanation.surface: A duenna takes tea with her young charge who is nearly grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is a chaperone to a young woman, so her duty is chaperonage, the act of escorting and supervising.

clue.text: Wellington's address offering telling punch — error mostly corrected

parts.note: KO, a knockout, is the most telling punch of all

indicators.note: a mistake that is corrected gets put into a different, proper order
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is cut

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: The Duke of Wellington makes a speech that lands a punch once its mistake is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington is not the duke but the capital of New Zealand, signalling a New Zealand word.
explanation.definitionFit: Korero is a New Zealand word, from Maori, for a talk, speech or discussion, so it is a form of address.

clue.text: Once prodigious energy, above standard

indicators.note: in a down entry, what comes above sits first, before the following piece

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a norm is a standard

explanation.surface: Remarkable energy, once above the usual level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Enorm is an archaic adjective meaning huge or enormous, which is what prodigious meant.

clue.text: Antiseptic compound? Unsuccessful one's given up, cocaine preferred

indicators.note: preferred is read as placed in front, so the drug comes first

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine

indicators.note: in a down entry, something given up is sent upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a loser is an unsuccessful person

explanation.surface: A failure gives up and turns to cocaine instead of an antiseptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Cresol is a coal-tar phenol compound used as a disinfectant and antiseptic.

clue.text: In Paris he boards Metro with me, switching device to record journey

indicators.note: to board a train is to get inside it, so one piece goes within the other
switching things around changes their order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged
il is French for he

explanation.surface: A Frenchman boards the Paris Metro with the narrator and switches on a gadget to log the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A milometer is the instrument in a vehicle that records the number of miles travelled.

clue.text: Election as part of formal account?

parts.note: in means included as part of something
a statement is a formal account, as given to police

explanation.surface: Is an election just one item in some official report?
explanation.definitionFit: Instatement is installing someone in office, which is what an election achieves.

clue.text: One in wellies quite likely kept in shoe rack

indicators.note: what is kept in something is stored within it, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A gardener's wellington boots are stored on the shoe rack.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellies are wellington boots, the rubber boots worn for muddy outdoor work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoer is someone working a garden with a hoe, a job usually done wearing rubber boots.

clue.text: Cartilaginous stuff in horn — CD's manufactured with it

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw materials, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A material found in horn is used in making compact discs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In horn' looks like a description of where the stuff is found, but the 'in' joins the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Chondrin is the gelatinous protein substance extracted from cartilage, so it is cartilaginous matter.

clue.text: Increase county gossip?

parts.note: county can mean upper-class, and U stands for upper-class
to prate is to chatter idly

explanation.surface: The talk of the shires keeps getting louder.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'county' describes the landed gentry, so it means upper-class; U is the label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To uprate is to raise a rate or value, so it is a verb meaning increase.

clue.text: Bird that's not OK in theater stalls?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, as seated inside the stalls

parts.note: in American theatres the parquet is the stalls

indicators.note: not here means without, so two letters are taken away from the bird

parts.note: a rook is a black crow-like bird
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A bird has got loose in the theatre seats, which is not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling 'theater' hints at the American term for the stalls. 'Bird' does double duty as definition and source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A parroquet is a variant spelling of parakeet, a small long-tailed parrot.

clue.text: Sets required in staging Elsinore

indicators.note: what is required in something is contained within it, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Sets are needed when putting on a play set at Elsinore, Hamlet's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets' looks like stage scenery, but it is a verb meaning to become firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly gels when it sets, firming from liquid to solid.

clue.text: Ships containing European in place of ordinary dabs

indicators.note: one thing in place of another replaces it, swapping one letter for another

parts.note: to ship goods abroad is to export them
E is the abbreviation for European
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A cargo of ordinary flatfish is sent out with a European aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dabs' looks like the flatfish, but it is the plural of dab, as in 'dab hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab, or dab hand, is a skilled person, so dabs are experts.

clue.text: Plain song? Probed endlessly about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other
without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to pry is to probe, and pried is its past tense
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Was it a plainsong that someone kept investigating?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain song' suggests plainsong chant; split apart, 'Plain' is the definition and 'song' supplies letters, with 'that' pointing back at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide, flat, treeless grassland, which is a plain.

clue.text: Muscly lump where contemporary art is shown round yard

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the museum is placed around the other letter

parts.note: MoMA is New York's Museum of Modern Art
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A muscular sculpture stands in a gallery courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A myoma is a benign tumour made of muscle tissue, so it is a lump of muscle.

clue.text: Doubly annoyed with service taken again for elaborate church symbol

parts.note: cross means annoyed, and doubly says to have it twice
in tennis a let is a serve that must be played again

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is twice as cross when the church service has to be repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a church service; it is a tennis serve. A let is called when a serve clips the net.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-crosslet is a heraldic cross whose four arms each end in a small cross, a fancy Christian emblem.

clue.text: Best tux restyled with oof

indicators.note: restyling something gives it a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dinner jacket is given a new look with cash to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: Oof is old slang for money, and a tux is a tuxedo.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or outwit them, which is what outfox means.

clue.text: Biddy entering coach for plane

indicators.note: what enters something goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a car is a railway carriage, or coach
biddy is a dialect word for a hen

explanation.surface: An old woman boards a coach to catch her flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft; it is the tree. Biddy suggests an old woman but means a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A chenar is the oriental plane tree of India and the Middle East.

clue.text: Sacred text, extract from scriptures as translated

indicators.note: an extract is a passage lifted out of a longer text, so the letters lie within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A holy book is quoted from scriptures in translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sastra, or shastra, is a Hindu scripture or treatise of sacred law.

clue.text: Domestic having to spray round centre of study

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the spray goes around the other letter

parts.note: to hose is to spray with water

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: A servant has to spray water around a study when cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like a household servant, but it is an adjective, as in house wine or house plant.
explanation.definitionFit: As a modifier, house means belonging to the home or the establishment itself, which is the sense of domestic.

clue.text: Priest welcoming church legate from overseas

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A priest receives a papal envoy visiting from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An elchi is a Turkish or Persian word for an ambassador or envoy, a foreign legate.

clue.text: Salt in love turned loose, worried

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: something turned is facing the other way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: lax means loose or slack
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: A lover set loose is fretting over a little salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' could be a sailor, but here it is a chemical salt.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxalate is a salt or ester of oxalic acid, so it is a salt in the chemical sense.

clue.text: Pressed to the mast, sailor's to work 'ard as drudge

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
to hack is to work as a drudge; 'ard signals the dropped H

explanation.surface: A sailor has to toil away like a drudge, dropping his aitches.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ard shows a Cockney dropped H, so the drudge's word loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails are aback when the wind presses them back against the mast, from the front.

clue.text: Gifts, on being removed from stock, sent off

indicators.note: what is removed from a word is taken out of it, leaving the rest

parts.note: in card games the talon is the stock, the undealt pile
taken as written, to be removed

indicators.note: off means gone bad or not right, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Presents taken out of the shop's stock are sent off by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like goods in a shop, but it is the card-game term for the undealt pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Talents are natural aptitudes, which are thought of as gifts.

clue.text: Strap cracks — time to leave

indicators.note: something told to leave goes away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: cracks are wisecracks, or jests
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A strap has cracked, so it's time to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A jess is a short strap fastened round a hawk's leg in falconry.

clue.text: What gets said after it, often recalling fine sport?

definitions.text: What gets said after it, often
definitions.note: a description of the word, which typically precedes 'said'

indicators.note: recalling is read as calling back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sport can mean fun or amusement
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something people often remark afterwards when reminiscing about a good game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuff said' is slang for 'enough said'; the definition describes the word as the one often followed by 'said'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuff is a slang spelling of enough, heard chiefly in the catchphrase nuff said.

clue.text: Calf that was butchered for Easter

indicators.note: butchered means cut up and mangled, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A calf was slaughtered for the Easter feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That was' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Steare is an old spelling of steer, a young bullock, so it once meant a young calf.

clue.text: Hay cooked with duck egg, soft inside — a morbid diet

indicators.note: inside places one letter within the others before they are mixed
cooking mixes ingredients up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, which looks like O
taken as written
P, for piano, means soft in music

explanation.surface: A meal of hay cooked with a soft-boiled duck egg sounds like an unhealthy diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Geophagy is the practice of eating earth or clay, often linked to a disorder, so it is an unhealthy diet.

clue.text: Survey serious corrosion affecting newbuild (beginnings of)

indicators.note: the beginnings of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: An inspector surveys a new building for bad corrosion at its foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Survey' is both the definition and the first of the four words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over or examine something carefully, which is to survey it.

clue.text: Source of timber set, bake furiously in brazier

parts.note: the fir is a tree grown for timber

indicators.note: doing something furiously means doing it wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Firewood is lit and burns fiercely in an outdoor heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebasket is an iron grate or cage for holding a fire, which is what a brazier is.
